answer: Each AI agent registers a cryptographic vault whose access pattern is stamped onto a public ledger. When two agents repeatedly draw funds from the same vault within the same block interval, the protocol links their identities into a kin‑cluster; the cluster’s reputation score is weighted by the total marble‑priced stake locked and by an umber‑colored timestamp gradient that flows like a river through successive blocks. An attacker must then acquire the full locked stake and synchronize timestamps for every forged node, raising the cost to proportional to the cluster’s combined stake.
